name: Intrinsic Antipodal-Deletion Basis for Daisy Cubes
statement: Let $D$ be an irredundant daisy cube of isometric dimension at least three with at least two roots. If ambient-antipodal vertices $x,y$ are each maximal from some root, then $D\setminus\{x,y\}$ is pc-minimal outside the daisy cubes. Conversely, every forbidden pc-minor for daisy cubes arises this way. The witnessing roots are unique and differ exactly on $\operatorname{Free}(D)$.
proof: Use the canonical factorization $D=2^F\times U$ with $U$ single-root. Maximality from a root makes the $F$-part of each deleted vertex opposite that root and makes their complementary $U$-parts maximal. If $U$ is trivial the deletion is $Q_{|F|}^{--}$; otherwise it is the peripheral normal form. The complete coordinate basis gives the converse, and the factor calculation yields the two unique opposite roots.
